# A01-S109: Artificial stupidity

Extract from the operator’s source text. Transport metadata, signatures and marked context omitted.

[…]

I’m slowly ready to reformulate the project, but it has to be able to contribute something to the company and my idea of what the company is has become somewhat weathered.

In another email, I have shared my working paper for an AI literature project with you, which I have tinkered with since last time. I thought if the future is uncertain, one better just start writing. It is written as a dissertation in the tradition of artistic research, showing how an AI would write Marcel Proust. In this way, I invert the question of whether an AI could write a great novel, and instead try to prove what kind of literature and thinking an AI (or an artificial stupidity) would itself think up.

It might interest you, and I hope to use it in the MindFuture context. It’s far from finished, missing a couple of hundred pages, but it’s quickly done.
